ModeMediaTip: Recognizes movies, TV series, anime and music in online databases, with metadata and release dates
ModeBatchTip: Any file: numbering, replacements, capitalization and other rules. Only the name changes
ModeBatchHint: Any file, with your own rules
DropHintMedia: Movies, TV series, anime and music are recognized automatically. Nothing changes until you confirm.
DropHintBatch: Any kind of file: photos, documents, music. Pick the rules and see the new names right away. Nothing changes until you confirm.
TitleLanguageTip: Title language: changing it restarts the lookups right away
DonateText: If you like the project and would like it to keep being updated and improved, and to see new projects come to life, buy the developer a coffee.
DonateNote: The button opens the PayPal donation form in your browser.
BatchFilterTip: Which files to rename: extensions (jpg png) or patterns with * and ? (IMG_*). Empty = all
SortOrderTip: The order in which files are numbered
NoRules: No rules yet: add one to see the new names.
RuleToggleTip: Turn this rule on or off
RuleNumberingDesc: Sequential number in the order chosen above. Digits 0 = automatic.
RuleNewNameDesc: One pattern for every file, e.g. "Holiday {n:000}" or "{date} {name}".
RuleReplaceDesc: Finds a text and replaces it (empty = removes it). With regular expressions use $1, $2…
RuleInsertDesc: Adds a text, also with placeholders like {date} or {folder}.
RuleRemoveCharsDesc: Removes characters by position (start, end, from a position) or by type (symbols, digits, uppercase…).
RuleCaseDesc: Changes the capitalization of the name (not of the extension).
RuleCleanupDesc: Removes separators, brackets, accents and double spaces.
RuleLettersToDigitsDesc: Replaces letters with look-alike numbers: “Bone Lake” ➔ “B0n3 L4k3”.
RuleExtensionDesc: Changes only the extension in the name: the file content is not converted.
RuleMoveDesc: Moves part of the name to the start, the end or after a given character.
RuleSwapDesc: Swaps the two parts around a separator: “Artist - Title” ➔ “Title - Artist”.
RuleRenumberDesc: Changes a number already in the name: a new sequence, or plus or minus a value.
RenumberDigitsTip: 0 = as many digits as the number had
RuleTrimDesc: Removes the chosen characters from the start and end, as long as it finds them.
RuleNameListDesc: One name per line, in file order. Empty lines keep the name as it is.
RuleReplaceListDesc: Several find and replace pairs, applied from top to bottom.
NumberingDigitsTip: Leading zeros: 3 = 001. With 0 the digits of the highest number are used
TokenWordHelp: second word of the name (-1 = the last)
TokenPartHelp: 4 characters from the first ({part:-4} = the last 4)
TokenRandomHelp: 4 random digits, fixed for each file
TokenResolutionHelp: width x height of photos and videos (also {width}, {height})
CreationDateHint: On this drive Linux does not allow changing the creation date of files: Renamr sets the modification date to the release date and, if enabled, also writes it into the embedded metadata. On NTFS drives mounted with ntfs-3g (Windows external drives) and on SMB network folders the creation date is changed.
DryRunTip: Rehearsal: checks permissions, locked files and conflicts without changing any file
WriteMetadataTip: Also writes metadata inside the files (MKV/MP4/MP3 tags); choose which fields in Settings. When off, Renamr only changes the name and the file dates.
IncludeLowConfidenceTip: Also renames files recognized with little certainty (yellow rows). Check them in the preview first.
SummaryDryRunMessage: {0} files would be renamed, {1} could not be. Nothing was changed: press Start Renaming to apply.
LanguageHintNoTmdb: Without a TMDb key movies are not recognized and TVmaze, the keyless source, has episode titles in English only: if the file name already contains one, Renamr keeps it. For titles in the chosen language ({0}) create a free key on themoviedb.org (Settings ➔ API) and paste it into the settings.
ProviderTmdbRejected: TMDb rejected the API key, so the titles came from other sources (in English). In Settings paste the "API Key" you find on themoviedb.org under Settings ➔ API.
ProviderKeyRejected: {0} rejected the API key: its results were replaced by other sources.
ProviderFailed: {0}: {1}, its results were replaced by other sources.
SettingsPlaceholders: Placeholders: {Title} {Year} {Resolution} {Show Title} {Season:00} {Episode:00} {Episode Title} {Absolute:000} {Artist} {Album} {Track:00}. Use / to organize into folders.
SettingsKeysHintWindows: Keys are encrypted with your Windows account. TVmaze and MusicBrainz work without a key; providers without a key are skipped.
SettingsKeysHintLinux: Keys are encrypted with a key readable only by your Linux user. TVmaze and MusicBrainz work without a key; providers without a key are skipped.
SettingsMetadataHint: Choose what Renamr writes to the files. Fields that are off stay as they are. "Write embedded metadata" in the main window turns all tags off at once.
MetaReleaseDate: Release year and date (also in the MKV/MP4 header)
MetaMusic: Music: artist, album and track number
SettingsBatchHint: API keys, name formats and recognition only apply to the "Movies, Series and Music" mode: switch to that mode to change them.
ErrorFileInUse: File in use by another process
ErrorReadOnlyNotCleared: Could not remove the Read-only attribute
ErrorTargetAlreadyExists: A file with the new name already exists
ErrorReparsePointRejected: Symbolic link or junction not allowed
ErrorInvalidFileName: The proposed name is not valid on Windows
ErrorProviderRateLimited: Too many requests to the online service, try again later
ErrorMetadataFormatUnsupported: Format does not support a date in its metadata
ErrorMetadataSkippedLargeFile: Embedded metadata not written: file over 4 GB
NameControlCharacter: The name contains a control character
NameBadCharacter: The character {0} is not allowed in file names
NameTrailingDot: The name cannot end with a dot or a space
PlanDuplicateTarget: Another file in the plan has the same destination name
BatchDuplicateTarget: The same name is already used by another file in the list
MetadataSkippedNoSpace: Embedded metadata not written: not enough space
MetadataSkippedSpace: not enough free space for the safety copy
MetadataSkippedDetail: {0}; the file dates are still set
MetadataSkippedHeader: {0}; the file dates are still set (date in the header: {1})
AddFilesTip: Add single files to the list, even from other folders
ChooseMatchTip: Click to pick from the results found or search for another title
MatchPickerNone: No results. Try searching with another title or type.
MatchPickerCount: {0} results: pick one and press “Use this”
